paras.zh: 因此，虽然杰西即将辞去他的官方职务，但我并不认为这意味着杰西离开了 Skydance。他帮助建造了这个地方。他是公司 DNA 的一部分。他将永远是这个家庭的一部分。

paras.en: Jesse, I don’t know that I can adequately thank you for everything you have done for Skydance – and for me – over the past decade. The company we are today simply would not exist without you. I’m incredibly proud of what we built, and even more grateful for the friendship that came with it.
paras.zh: 杰西，我不知道我该如何充分感谢你在过去十年中为 Skydance 以及为我所做的一切。如果没有你们，我们今天的公司就不会存在。我对我们所建立的一切感到无比自豪，更感激随之而来的友谊。

paras.en: I can’t wait to see what you do next – and look forward to all that we’ll continue to do together in the future.
paras.zh: 我迫不及待地想看看你下一步会做什么——并期待着我们未来继续一起做的一切。

articles.title: ‘Inside the NBA’ Host Ernie Johnson Says This Is His Final Season
articles.author: Rick Porter

paras.en: Ernie Johnson, the long-serving host of Inside the NBA on TNT and ESPN, is stepping down.
paras.zh: TNT 和 ESPN 的《Inside the NBA》长期担任主持人厄尼·约翰逊 (Ernie Johnson) 即将辞职。

paras.en: In an Instagram video Wednesday, Johnson said that this season — his 37th — will be his last as the host of the NBA highlights and analysis show. Johnson became host of Inside the NBA with its second season in 1990 and has been at the helm ever since, wrangling and playing off of analysts Kenny Smith (since 1998), Charles Barkley (since 2000) and Shaquille O’Neal (since 2011).
paras.zh: 周三，约翰逊在 Instagram 视频中表示，本赛季——他的第 37 个赛季——将是他主持 NBA 集锦和分析节目的最后一个赛季。约翰逊于 1990 年成为《Inside the NBA》第二季的主持人，此后一直掌舵，与分析师肯尼·史密斯（自 1998 年起）、查尔斯·巴克利（自 2000 年起）和沙奎尔·奥尼尔（自 2011 年起）争论和较量。

paras.en: “I’ve long described it as a ‘get to’ job — I’m still amazed I get to do this for a living,” Johnson said in the video (watch it in full below). “… This will be my last season. It’s totally my decision. It’s just time.”
paras.zh: “长期以来，我一直将其描述为一份‘开始’的工作——我仍然很惊讶我能以此为生，”约翰逊在视频中说道（请在下面观看完整视频）。 “……这将是我的最后一个赛季。这完全是我的决定。只是时间而已。”

paras.en: Johnson also said that he has taken pride in how well he prepares for each show, but “I’ve always vowed that if ever became more of a challenge than it is a joy, then I’ll know it’s time to step away. Now after 37 seasons, it’s time.”
paras.zh: 约翰逊还表示，他为自己为每场演出所做的充分准备感到自豪，但“我一直发誓，如果挑战变得大于乐趣，那么我就会知道是时候离开了。37 季过去了，现在是时候了。”

paras.en: Barkley pre-empted Johnson’s announcement somewhat in September, saying that he planned to retire from Inside the NBA alongside Johnson after the 2026-27 season. “Right now, unless Ernie changes his mind, next year is my last year for 100%,” Barkley said on The Bill Simmons Podcast.
paras.zh: 巴克利在 9 月份抢先了约翰逊的声明，表示他计划在 2026-27 赛季结束后与约翰逊一起从 NBA 退役。 “现在，除非厄尼改变主意，否则明年是我百分百努力的最后一年，”巴克利在比尔·西蒙斯播客上说道。

paras.en: In his announcement, Johnson also cited some recent health issues “a contributing factor” in his decision. The 70-year-old Johnson had heart bypass surgery in 2025, and while he said he feels “great” and isn’t under doctor’s orders to scale back, he wants to use more of his time to be with his family, including his five grandchildren.
paras.zh: 约翰逊在声明中还提到了最近的一些健康问题是他做出决定的“一个促成因素”。 70 岁的约翰逊于 2025 年接受了心脏搭桥手术，虽然他说自己感觉“很好”，并且医生没有要求他缩减手术规模，但他希望用更多的时间陪伴家人，包括他的五个孙子。

paras.en: Inside the NBA was TNT’s signature show covering the league from 1989-2025. When TNT lost rights to the NBA after the 2024-25 season, ESPN picked up the show and airs it during select nights of its NBA coverage on ESPN and ABC. TNT Sports continues to produce the show and licenses it to ESPN.
paras.zh: NBA 内部是 TNT 的标志性节目，涵盖 1989 年至 2025 年的联盟。当 TNT 在 2024-25 赛季结束后失去 NBA 转播权时，ESPN 接手了该节目，并在 ESPN 和 ABC 的 NBA 报道的特定夜晚播出。 TNT Sports 继续制作该节目并将其授权给 ESPN。

paras.en: Johnson isn’t fully retiring: He’ll still be part of NCAA basketball coverage on TNT and has a production company, 32 Bow Ties.
paras.zh: 约翰逊并未完全退休：他仍将出现在 TNT 的 NCAA 篮球报道中，并拥有一家制作公司 32 Bow Ties。

paras.en: “Ernie Johnson has been and always will be the heart and soul of TNT Sports. He’s a legend in every sense — as a broadcaster and iconic host of Inside the NBA to being a world-class person who is beloved by all,” TNT Sports said in a statement. “With his decision to step back from Inside the NBA, we look forward to partnering with him on his next chapter at TNT Sports.”
paras.zh: TNT Sports 在一份声明中表示：“厄尼·约翰逊一直是、也将永远是 TNT Sports 的核心和灵魂。从各个方面来说，他都是一位传奇人物——从《Inside the NBA》的播音员和标志性主持人，到受到所有人喜爱的世界级人物。” “随着他决定退出 Inside NBA，我们期待与他合作，开启 TNT Sports 的下一个篇章。”

articles.title: Anthropic IPO filing warns some risks may be uninsurable. AI coverage will be issue for every company

paras.en: Anthropic's IPO filing includes many words covering many risks, from IP theft to security incidents, data loss, climate change, rogue agents and all the way to an existential crisis for humanity. Embedded in all of the risk language are basic questions about insurance: What's going to be covered? Is it even possible to provide a policy for all of the ways that AI could go wrong? Anthropic, even with more cash than almost any company in America, couldn't answer that question with confidence.
paras.zh: Anthropic 的 IPO 文件包含许多词汇，涵盖多种风险，从知识产权盗窃到安全事件、数据丢失、气候变化、流氓特工，一直到人类的生存危机。所有风险语言中都包含有关保险的基本问题：承保什么？是否有可能为人工智能可能出错的所有方式提供政策？尽管 Anthropic 拥有比美国几乎所有公司都多的现金，但仍无法自信地回答这个问题。

paras.en: "Because our models may behave in ways that no user or developer intended, claims arising from such actions could result in substantial liability. Our insurance policies also may not provide sufficient coverage to adequately mitigate the potential liabilities we face, especially where any one incident, or a group of incidents, causes disproportionate harm," the company's S-1 filing states. "In addition, with the scale of harm that could result from a catastrophic AI-related incident, no single insurer, and potentially the insurance industry in the aggregate, may have sufficient capacity or expertise to underwrite insurance commensurate with such exposure. Further, the insurance market for AI-specific risks is nascent and evolving, and we may be unable to obtain coverage for certain AI-related liabilities on commercially reasonable terms, or at all, leaving us exposed to potentially significant uninsured losses."
paras.zh: “由于我们的模型可能会以非用户或开发人员预期的方式运行，因此此类行为引起的索赔可能会导致重大责任。我们的保险单也可能无法提供足够的承保范围来充分减轻我们面临的潜在责任，特别是在任何一个事件或一组事件造成不成比例的损害的情况下，”该公司的 S-1 文件指出。 “此外，鉴于灾难性人工智能相关事件可能造成的损害规模，没有任何一家保险公司，甚至可能是整个保险业，可能有足够的能力或专业知识来承保与此类风险相称的保险。此外，人工智能特定风险的保险市场尚处于萌芽状态并不断发展，我们可能无法以商业合理的条款获得某些人工智能相关责任的承保，或者根本无法使我们面临潜在的重大未投保损失。”

paras.en: Those risks are far removed from AI chatbots helping to book airline tickets or find the best deals on a backyard grill. But there have been increasing instances where AI chatbots are going rogue and some companies are watching warily — even blocking them. In some extreme cases, chatbots are being accused of contributing to a death, including a case revealed this week, raising insurance questions for which there are no easy answers. And with AI starting to permeate seemingly every part of every business ecosystem, the risk of exposure and liability connected to AI continues to increase, and that has the insurance industry on alert.
paras.zh: 这些风险与帮助预订机票或在后院烧烤找到最优惠价格的人工智能聊天机器人相去甚远。但人工智能聊天机器人失控的情况越来越多，一些公司正在警惕地观察，甚至阻止它们。在一些极端的情况下，聊天机器人被指控造成死亡，包括本周披露的一起案件，引发了一些没有简单答案的保险问题。随着人工智能开始渗透到每个商业生态系统的几乎每个部分，与人工智能相关的风险和责任风险持续增加，这引起了保险业的警惕。

paras.en: Alissa Lugo, a senior director analyst in Gartner's legal & compliance practice, says her research shows "death by AI" claims could exceed 2,000 worldwide by end of 2026 — defined as cases in which AI played some role in a fatality, and that number is expected to grow.
paras.zh: Gartner 法律与合规业务高级总监分析师 Alissa Lugo 表示，她的研究显示，到 2026 年底，全球范围内“人工智能导致死亡”的索赔可能会超过 2000 起——定义为人工智能在死亡事件中发挥了一定作用的案例，而且这一数字预计还会增长。

paras.en: Lugo says more companies are building in AI exclusions, and that ultimately insurers, with assistance from the courts, will decide the parameters of AI coverage and how it fits in. Claims for bodily injury, in particular, are where cyber insurance coverage gets thin.
paras.zh: 卢戈表示，越来越多的公司正在建立人工智能除外责任，最终保险公司将在法院的协助下决定人工智能承保范围的参数及其适应方式。特别是人身伤害索赔，是网络保险承保范围薄弱的领域。

paras.en: Many experts, including Lugo, compare AI liability today to the early days of cyber insurance.
paras.zh: 包括卢戈在内的许多专家将当今的人工智能责任与早期的网络保险进行了比较。

paras.en: "Right now, cyber is the policy doing the most to cover AI, but it only covers one kind of AI loss. Cyber responds when AI is involved in a data breach, a privacy violation, a system outage, or a deepfake wire fraud," said Dennis Hendrickson of Hendrickson Insurance, an independent brokerage in Sarasota, Florida.
paras.zh: 佛罗里达州萨拉索塔独立经纪公司 Hendrickson Insurance 的丹尼斯·亨德里克森 (Dennis Hendrickson) 表示：“目前，网络保险是对人工智能承保最多的保险，但它只承保一种人工智能损失。当人工智能涉及数据泄露、侵犯隐私、系统中断或深度伪造电汇欺诈时，网络就会做出反应。”

paras.en: Hendrickson noted that some cyber carriers have widened their wording to include AI-driven security events. "That's useful. But nearly every cyber policy excludes bodily injury. Cyber was built for data and dollars, not for people getting hurt. This is where there is a major problem, in my opinion," he said, calling the lack of bodily injury or physical damage coverage a "gaping hole" that will need to be addressed.
paras.zh: 亨德里克森指出，一些网络运营商已经扩大了措辞，将人工智能驱动的安全事件包括在内。 “这很有用。但几乎每项网络政策都排除人身伤害。网络是为了数据和金钱而建立的，而不是为了人们受伤。在我看来，这是一个主要问题。”他说，缺乏人身伤害或物理损坏保险是一个需要解决的“漏洞”。

paras.en: Kara Higginbotham, head of professional liability and cyber for U.S. national accounts at Zurich North America, says AI is creating new exposures across various product lines, but how insurers are navigating it varies greatly by line of business. "Every line of business is handling things a bit differently," she said.
paras.zh: 苏黎世北美公司美国国民账户专业责任和网络主管卡拉·希金博瑟姆 (Kara Higginbotham) 表示，人工智能正在各个产品线中创造新的风险，但保险公司如何驾驭它，因业务线而异。 “每个行业的处理方式都略有不同，”她说。

paras.en: Some companies, including Zurich, have a suite of approved AI tools for workers to use, while others are blocked, and she said safeguards may have to be built into policies as a matter of course for AI protection going forward. But for now, she said, a gap still generally exists in coverage when it comes to bodily harm or physical harm from an AI-related incident.
paras.zh: 包括苏黎世在内的一些公司拥有一套经过批准的人工智能工具供员工使用，而其他公司则被封锁，她表示，为了未来的人工智能保护，可能必须将保障措施纳入政策中。但她表示，目前，在涉及人工智能相关事件造成的人身伤害或身体伤害时，保险范围仍普遍存在差距。

paras.en: "It is a gap because it is not being covered by default. A lot of carriers would be wary to write that into a policy today, because as carriers, we have to be able to underwrite risk," Higginbotham said, noting that these are scenarios that are too new and not understood well enough yet, though general liability could in some cases be extended to cover them.
paras.zh: “这是一个缺口，因为它没有被默认覆盖。今天，许多承运人会谨慎地将其写入保单，因为作为承运人，我们必须能够承保风险，”希金博特姆说。他指出，这些情况太新了，还没有得到充分理解，尽管在某些情况下，一般责任可以扩展到涵盖这些情况。

paras.en: "Insurers are saying, 'We can't cover what you can't show us.' Most companies can't say where their employees are using AI tools. That's the first thing to fix," said Henrietta Akpata, executive fellow and visiting professional lecturer of management and AI at Marist University.
paras.zh: “保险公司说，‘我们无法承保您无法向我们展示的内容。’大多数公司无法透露其员工在哪里使用人工智能工具。这是首先要解决的问题，”玛丽斯特大学执行研究员兼管理和人工智能客座专业讲师 Henrietta Akpata 说。

paras.en: Akpata says this isn't just a problem for big tech companies. A local business whose website chatbot gives a customer the wrong answer, or an HR team using AI to sort job applications, could run into issues. "Those are everyday uses, and they may no longer be covered," Akpata says.
paras.zh: 阿克帕塔表示，这不仅仅是大型科技公司面临的问题。网站聊天机器人向客户提供错误答案的本地企业，或者使用人工智能对工作申请进行分类的人力资源团队，都可能会遇到问题。 “这些都是日常用途，可能不再涵盖在内，”阿克帕塔说。

paras.en: Experts seem divided as to whether AI insurance will evolve into a widespread separate product or be folded into existing cyber policies. Hendrickson says financial-loss AI coverage will become routine and priced like cyber. Bodily injury from AI will be the hard line. Expect tight underwriting, low sub-limits, and requirements for a human to review what the AI does before it reaches a patient. Some healthcare-adjacent businesses won't be able to buy it at all, insurance experts say.
paras.zh: 对于人工智能保险是否会发展成为一种广泛应用的独立产品，还是纳入现有的网络保单，专家们似乎存在分歧。亨德里克森表示，人工智能的经济损失保险将成为常态，其定价将像网络保险一样。人工智能造成的身体伤害将是强硬路线。预计承保会很严格，次限额较低，并且要求人类在人工智能到达患者手中之前检查其所做的事情。保险专家表示，一些与医疗保健相关的企业根本无法购买它。

paras.en: Jaymin Kim, who leads emerging technologies in Marsh's cyber practice, says that so far the firm isn't seeing a ton of AI claims, and she believes that AI issues should be handled within existing insurance policies — including cyber, media, casualty, and first party insurance, among others — though underwriting guidelines and pricing, among other factors, may need to be adjusted. "AI is not a peril. It's just a technology through which existing familiar categories of harms and losses might manifest," said Kim, who noted that trying to separate out AI into its own insurance category could be very tedious.
paras.zh: 达信网络业务新兴技术负责人 Jaymin Kim 表示，到目前为止，该公司还没有看到大量人工智能索赔，她认为人工智能问题应该在现有保险保单内处理——包括网络保险、媒体保险、伤亡保险和第一方保险等——尽管承保指南和定价等因素可能需要调整。 “人工智能不是一种危险。它只是一种技术，通过它可能会体现出现有的熟悉的伤害和损失类别，”金说，他指出，试图将人工智能分离到自己的保险类别中可能会非常乏味。

paras.en: "We're increasingly seeing AI being embedded in everyday business activities, and so by virtue of that, it's becoming invisible and ubiquitous. Which means on the insurance side, you cannot practically isolate AI in the causal chain of loss," Kim said. She added that just because AI happened to be involved in a data privacy event or a security event, it's still a data privacy or security event. She added that managing competing policies could be a nightmare for a customer.
paras.zh: “我们越来越多地看到人工智能被嵌入到日常商业活动中，因此，它变得无形且无处不在。这意味着在保险方面，你实际上无法将人工智能与损失的因果链隔离开来，”金说。她补充说，仅仅因为人工智能碰巧涉及数据隐私事件或安全事件，它仍然是数据隐私或安全事件。她补充说，管理竞争政策对客户来说可能是一场噩梦。

paras.en: "Are we saying now we're going to have one CGL policy for everything that doesn't touch AI, and then a second CGL policy for everything that does touch AI?" Kim said.
paras.zh: “我们现在是不是说，我们将为所有不涉及人工智能的事物制定一项 CGL 政策，然后为所有涉及人工智能的事物制定第二项 CGL 政策？”金说。

paras.en: The industry has not yet seen a wholly new category of risk created by AI, but Kim conceded, "maybe the operative word is 'yet.'"
paras.zh: 该行业尚未看到人工智能带来的全新风险类别，但 Kim 承认，“也许最重要的词是‘还’。”

paras.en: What cyber insurance history says about the AI risk future
paras.zh: 网络保险的历史如何看待人工智能风险的未来

paras.en: Vikram Desai, global cyber strategy, risk and architecture lead at Accenture, said that until recently, every conversation was about getting AI into the business. "Now, it's about what happens when it goes wrong. That's exposed how badly AI fits the policies companies already own," Desai said.
paras.zh: 埃森哲全球网络战略、风险和架构主管维克拉姆·德赛 (Vikram Desai) 表示，直到最近，每次讨论都在讨论将人工智能引入业务。 “现在，问题在于出现问题时会发生什么。这暴露了人工智能与公司已有政策的契合程度有多差，”德赛说。

paras.en: In some respects, that is similar to the early days of cybersecurity. "Cyber risk sat silently inside general liability for years until insurers named it, excluded it, then sold it back. AI is on the same curve, but compressed," Desai said. "The real exposure is the AI companies don't know they have. Exclusions can bite when AI sits anywhere in the causal chain, including inside a vendor's product," Desai added.
paras.zh: 在某些方面，这类似于网络安全的早期阶段。 “多年来，网络风险一直默默地存在于一般责任范围内，直到保险公司将其命名、排除在外，然后将其卖回。人工智能处于同一曲线上，但受到压缩，”德赛说。 “真正的暴露是人工智能公司不知道自己已经暴露了。当人工智能位于因果链的任何位置时，包括在供应商的产品中，排除可能会产生影响，”德赛补充道。

paras.en: He says underwriters are already asking where AI is being used and who is overseeing it.
paras.zh: 他说，承销商已经在询问人工智能在哪里使用以及由谁来监督。

paras.en: Higginbotham said most of the AI-related claims being made today don't involve headline-grabbing, network-shutdown-type attacks, but rather more pedestrian claims around intellectual property — primarily against AI developers accused of scraping content used to train the model, or infringement claims alleging an AI model was trained on copyrighted content. "We also have seen data misuse or privacy-related claims," Higginbotham said.
paras.zh: Higginbotham 表示，今天提出的大多数与人工智能相关的索赔并不涉及引人注目的网络关闭类型的攻击，而是围绕知识产权的平淡索赔——主要针对被指控抓取用于训练模型的内容的人工智能开发人员，或指控人工智能模型接受受版权保护的内容训练的侵权索赔。 “我们还看到了数据滥用或与隐私相关的索赔，”希金博特姆说。

paras.en: One complication is that on the cyber side, it isn't always immediately apparent whether AI was used in a social engineering attack — for instance, someone sending an email or Teams message impersonating a colleague.
paras.zh: 一个复杂的问题是，在网络方面，人工智能是否被用于社会工程攻击并不总是立即显而易见——例如，有人冒充同事发送电子邮件或 Teams 消息。

paras.en: "We know that bad actors are using AI in more convincing ways to carry out attacks, and that is buoying cyber claims, accelerating them," Higginbotham said, but she added that it isn't always clear what role AI played. "So it will not be a separate category," she said, adding that cyber insurance is designed to handle this kind of exposure.
paras.zh: 希金博瑟姆说：“我们知道，不良行为者正在以更令人信服的方式利用人工智能来实施攻击，这助长了网络索赔，加速了攻击的发生。”但她补充说，人工智能扮演的角色并不总是很清楚。 “所以这不会是一个单独的类别，”她说，并补充说网络保险旨在应对这种风险。

paras.en: She says that if the insurer sees "a sustained change in claim development patterns," it may have to start charging more for the coverage if it presents issues for the balance sheet from loss exposure, "but we are not there yet," she added.
paras.zh: 她表示，如果保险公司看到“索赔发展模式持续发生变化”，如果损失风险给资产负债表带来问题，它可能不得不开始收取更高的承保费用，“但我们还没有做到这一点，”她补充道。

paras.en: "Our underwriting will have to evolve and adapt to changes in the threat environment. We are currently working on partnering with law firms and tech vendors to help," Higginbotham said. "We are not always looking to exclude the next risk — we want to help companies manage risk," she said.
paras.zh: “我们的承保必须不断发展并适应威胁环境的变化。我们目前正在与律师事务所和技术供应商合作提供帮助，”希金博瑟姆说。 “我们并不总是寻求排除下一个风险——我们希望帮助公司管理风险，”她说。

paras.en: Companies that have not implemented baseline controls may eventually be subject to exclusions if they prove unwilling to change their risk management approach. "But we don't jump to exclusions as the first arrow in the quiver," Higginbotham said.
paras.zh: 尚未实施基线控制的公司如果被证明不愿意改变其风险管理方法，最终可能会被排除在外。 “但我们不会把排除作为第一支箭，”希金博特姆说。

paras.en: Hendrickson, like others, is seeing parallels to cyber insurance, and he says he is waiting for the deluge of claims that he is certain is coming, and that he says no one is prepared for, including the large carriers.
paras.zh: 亨德里克森和其他人一样，看到了网络保险的相似之处，他说他正在等待他确信即将到来的大量索赔，但他说没有人做好准备，包括大型运营商。

paras.en: "We've seen this before with cyber insurance. First insurers stopped covering it, then they created separate policies for it, and their checklists ended up setting the rules companies followed. I expect the same with AI: for many businesses, insurers will set the standards before the government does," he said.
paras.zh: “我们之前在网络保险中就看到过这种情况。首先保险公司停止承保，然后他们为其制定了单独的保单，他们的清单最终制定了公司遵循的规则。我预计人工智能也是如此：对于许多企业来说，保险公司将在政府之前制定标准，”他说。

paras.en: "Insurance companies come out with a new product, then the claims come in, and they won't renew the policy," Hendrickson said, adding that it's often independent agents like him left bearing the brunt from irate or uncovered customers. "We're the ones in the trenches dealing with this every day."
paras.zh: 亨德里克森说：“保险公司推出了新产品，然后提出索赔，他们就不会续签保单。”他补充说，通常是像他这样的独立代理人首当其冲地承受着愤怒或未获保障的客户的损失。 “我们每天都在第一线处理这个问题。”

paras.en: Correction: Jaymin Kim, who leads emerging technologies in Marsh's cyber practice, believes that AI issues should be handled within existing insurance policies — including cyber, media, casualty, and first party insurance, among others. An earlier version of this article mischaracterized her assessment.
paras.zh: 更正：达信网络业务新兴技术负责人 Jaymin Kim 认为，人工智能问题应在现有保险政策内处理，包括网络、媒体、伤亡和第一方保险等。本文的早期版本错误地描述了她的评估。

articles.title: Watch live: Fed Chairman Warsh explains why the central bank paused rate hikes

paras.en: The Federal Reserve held steady on rates at the conclusion of its October meeting, maintaining its target range of 3.75% to 4%. The move was widely anticipated by the market.
paras.zh: 美联储在 10 月份会议结束时维持利率不变，维持 3.75% 至 4% 的目标区间。此举受到市场广泛预期。

paras.en: Two members of the Federal Open Market Committee dissented from the decision: Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack were in favor of raising rates by a quarter percentage point.
paras.zh: 联邦公开市场委员会的两名成员对这一决定持反对意见：州长丽莎·库克和克利夫兰联储主席贝丝·哈马克赞成加息四分之一个百分点。

paras.en: Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh will discuss the central bank's latest rate decision at a press conference scheduled for 2:30 p.m. ET.
paras.zh: 美联储主席凯文·沃什 (Kevin Warsh) 将在定于下午 2:30 举行的新闻发布会上讨论央行的最新利率决定。等。

paras.en: Traders have shifted their focus to the December meeting, where fed funds futures trading implies a roughly 85% likelihood of a rate hike, according to the CME FedWatch tool.
paras.zh: 交易员已将注意力转向 12 月会议，根据 CME FedWatch 工具，联邦基金期货交易意味着加息的可能性约为 85%。

articles.title: S&P 500 remains higher as Fed leaves rates steady: Live updates

paras.en: The S&P 500 rose on Wednesday as investors reacted to the Federal Reserve's latest interest rate decision and awaited earnings reports from mega-cap technology companies.
paras.zh: 由于投资者对美联储最新利率决定做出反应并等待大型科技公司的盈利报告，标准普尔 500 指数周三上涨。

paras.en: The broad market index gained 0.1%, while the Nasdaq Composite traded down 0.1%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 82 points, or 0.2%.
paras.zh: 大盘指数上涨 0.1%，而纳斯达克综合指数下跌 0.1%。道琼斯工业平均指数上涨 82 点，即 0.2%。

paras.en: The Fed kept interest rates steady at a target rate range of 3.75% to 4%. Policymakers had raised rates by a quarter percentage point at their September meeting, marking its first hike since 2023.
paras.zh: 美联储将利率稳定在3.75%至4%的目标利率区间。政策制定者在 9 月份的会议上将利率提高了四分之一个百分点，这是自 2023 年以来的首次加息。

paras.en: "The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2 percent goal," the Fed said in its post-meeting statement.
paras.zh: 美联储在会后声明中表示：“积累更多信息将有助于委员会确定适当的政策立场，以确保通胀及时回到委员会2%的目标。”

paras.en: Traders had widely anticipated the move. Heading into Wednesday's meeting, fed funds futures trading priced in a nearly 93% chance that the central bank would maintain the current interest rate, per CME's FedWatch tool.
paras.zh: 交易员普遍预期此举。根据 CME 的 FedWatch 工具，在周三的会议之前，联邦基金期货交易定价了央行维持当前利率的可能性近 93%。

paras.en: "We expect the Fed to resume rate hikes in December," said Kay Haigh, global head and CIO of fixed income and liquidity solutions at Goldman Sachs Asset Management. "September's strong CPI print is a reminder that upside inflation risks remain, and the Fed is likely to look to take out further insurance. While the September dot-plot suggests just one more hike, another increase in energy prices or further strong data prints could bring additional tightening into play next year."
paras.zh: 高盛资产管理公司固定收益和流动性解决方案全球主管兼首席信息官Kay Haigh表示：“我们预计美联储将在12月恢复加息。” “9月份强劲的CPI数据提醒人们，上行通胀风险依然存在，美联储可能会考虑采取进一步的保险措施。虽然9月份的点阵图表明只是再次加息，但能源价格的再次上涨或进一步强劲的数据数据可能会在明年带来额外的紧缩政策。”

paras.en: U.S. chipmakers moved higher Wednesday, buoyed by SK Hynix posting record quarterly profit — a development that sent U.S. shares of the South Korean chipmaker up 13%. Micron Technology was up 4%, while Arm Holdings advanced 3%. Marvell Technology moved up more than 2%, and Advanced Micro Devices increased around 2%.
paras.zh: 受 SK 海力士公布创纪录季度利润的提振，美国芯片制造商周三走高，这一进展导致这家韩国芯片制造商的美国股价上涨 13%。美光科技 (Micron Technology) 上涨 4%，Arm Holdings 上涨 3%。 Marvell Technology 上涨超过 2%，Advanced Micro Devices 上涨约 2%。

paras.en: Investors' attention will remain on the artificial intelligence trade after the bell, as "Magnificent Seven" giants Alphabet and Microsoft are set to report their latest quarterly results. The former was last seen up more than 1%, while the latter was down nearly 1%.
paras.zh: 盘后投资者的注意力仍将集中在人工智能交易上，“七大巨头”Alphabet 和微软将公布最新季度业绩。前者上涨超过 1%，而后者则下跌近 1%。

paras.en: Tech stocks, particularly those with exposure to the AI buildout, have struggled in recent weeks amid questions over the technology's financing.
paras.zh: 科技股，尤其是那些涉足人工智能领域的股票，最近几周因技术融资问题而陷入困境。

paras.en: "The near-term cycle remains incredibly healthy," said Bill Northey, investment director at U.S. Bank Asset Management Group. "It's really about can it remain durable for many years, and what are the returns to those who are investing significantly today. Will it be universally a profitable endeavor, or will there start to be some winners and losers that emerge there, and we tend to think that it leans towards the latter."
paras.zh: 合众银行资产管理集团投资总监比尔·诺西表示：“近期周期仍然非常健康。” “这实际上是关于它能否保持多年的耐用性，以及那些今天进行大量投资的人的回报是什么。它会是普遍有利可图的努力，还是会开始出现一些赢家和输家，我们倾向于认为它倾向于后者。”

articles.title: Animal-borne Shamonda virus infects and kills a human for the first time

paras.en: A person has contracted and died from the Shamonda virus, a disease-causing microbe that had been thought to only infect animals, for the first time. The incident, while unlikely to herald a more widespread outbreak, is a potent reminder of the potential for pathogens to jump from animals to humans—with deadly consequences.
paras.zh: 首次有人感染沙蒙达病毒并死亡，这种致病微生物曾被认为只会感染动物。这一事件虽然不太可能预示着更广泛的疫情爆发，但却有力地提醒人们，病原体有可能从动物传染给人类，从而造成致命的后果。

paras.en: The Shamonda virus was first identified in cattle in Nigeria in 1965. Spread by bites from tiny insects called Culicoides midges, it causes several symptoms in the animals, including fever, diarrhea and reduced milk production. The virus has also been known to infect sheep, goats, horses and alpacas. Previously, cases have been detected in some African countries, Japan and—for the first time this summer—Europe. But the virus doesn’t even seem overly contagious and isn’t deadly in adult animals. (Infected pregnant animals can transmit it to their fetus, however, which can result in miscarriage, stillbirth or birth defects.)
paras.zh: 沙蒙达病毒于 1965 年首次在尼日利亚的牛身上发现。该病毒通过库蠓这种微小昆虫的叮咬传播，会导致动物出现多种症状，包括发烧、腹泻和产奶量减少。据了解，这种病毒还会感染绵羊、山羊、马和羊驼。此前，一些非洲国家、日本和欧洲（今年夏天首次）发现了病例。但这种病毒似乎没有过度传染性，对成年动物也不是致命的。 （然而，受感染的怀孕动物可以将其传播给胎儿，这可能导致流产、死产或出生缺陷。）

paras.en: Yet for the first time in the more than six decades since it was discovered, Shamonda was detected in humans. A 61-year-old man who was undergoing treatment for leukemia at the Civil Hospital of Lyon in France contracted the disease. According to a case report published in Eurosurveillance, the man had undergone a stem cell transplant and experienced fatal encephalitis, or brain swelling. He showed symptoms, such as blindness and confusion, that the report authors say were likely caused by the virus. The man fell into a coma and succumbed to the disease on October 9, 2026, after life support was withdrawn. He is the first person ever known to have contracted the disease and died as a result. There are no vaccines to protect animals or people from Shamonda infections.
paras.zh: 然而，自从发现沙蒙达以来的六十多年来，这是第一次在人体中检测到沙蒙达。一名61岁男子在法国里昂市民医院接受白血病治疗时染病。根据《欧洲监视》发表的一份病例报告，该男子接受了干细胞移植，并出现了致命性脑炎或脑肿胀。他表现出了失明和精神错乱等症状，报告作者称这些症状很可能是由病毒引起的。 2026年10月9日，该男子陷入昏迷，在生命维持系统被撤除后去世。他是已知的第一个感染这种疾病并因此死亡的人。没有疫苗可以保护动物或人免受沙蒙达感染。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Experts emphasize the need for caution. “At this stage, there is no evidence that the Shamonda virus will become more common in humans,” says clinical virologist Grégory Destras. He is affiliated with the same hospital in Lyon and is a co-author of the report. Destras notes that the virus may have spent several weeks incubating and multiplying in the patient before the neurological symptoms appeared.
paras.zh: 专家强调需要谨慎。临床病毒学家格雷戈里·德斯特拉斯（Grégory Destras）表示：“现阶段，没有证据表明沙蒙达病毒会在人类中变得更加常见。”他隶属于里昂同一家医院，并且是该报告的合著者。德斯特拉斯指出，在出现神经系统症状之前，病毒可能已经在患者体内潜伏和繁殖了数周时间。

paras.en: In a joint statement, the French Ministry of Health and Ministry of Agriculture said that they suspect the patient contracted the disease from a midge bite in eastern France, where the disease has been found in several animals. Officials have reported their findings to the World Health Organization and the European Center for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC).
paras.zh: 法国卫生部和农业部在一份联合声明中表示，他们怀疑该患者是在法国东部被蠓叮咬后感染的，该地区的几只动物身上都发现了这种疾病。官员们已向世界卫生组织和欧洲疾病预防和控制中心（ECDC）报告了他们的发现。

paras.en: Shamonda has been found in livestock in 14 European countries. Two new clades of the virus, SHAV-EU1 and SHAV-EU2, were detected earlier this year, and genetic testing revealed traces of the first type in the deceased person’s cerebrospinal fluid, urine and saliva, among other samples.
paras.zh: 沙蒙达已在 14 个欧洲国家的牲畜中被发现。今年早些时候检测到了该病毒的两个新分支：SHAV-EU1 和 SHAV-EU2，基因检测在死者的脑脊液、尿液和唾液等样本中发现了第一种病毒的痕迹。

paras.en: The Shamonda virus is part of the Simbu serogroup and belongs to the genus Orthobunyavirus—the same serogroup and genus as the Oropouche virus, or sloth fever, which caused 9.4 million human infections in Latin America and the Caribbean regions from 1960 to 2025.
paras.zh: 沙蒙达病毒是辛布血清群的一部分，属于正布尼亚病毒属，与奥罗普切病毒或树懒热属于同一血清群和属，后者从 1960 年到 2025 年在拉丁美洲和加勒比地区造成了 940 万人感染。

paras.en: Indiana University School of Medicine virologist Natasha Tilston-Lunel highlights the Oropouche cases, but notes that the Schmallenberg virus, which is closely related to Shamonda, has been found to be widespread in livestock but not humans. She believes that, based on current information, Shamonda may also have limited infectiousness among people. Continued surveillance of livestock and their aborted fetuses, insects and genomic sequencing of human samples, however, will be critical to detecting any changes to Shamonda’s risk in people, she says. Tilston-Lunel was not associated with the new study.
paras.zh: 印第安纳大学医学院病毒学家 Natasha Tilston-Lunel 强调了奥罗普奇病例，但指出与 Shamonda 密切相关的施马伦伯格病毒已被发现在家畜中广泛传播，但在人类中并不存在。她认为，根据目前的信息，沙蒙达在人与人之间的传染性可能也有限。然而，她说，对牲畜及其流产胎儿、昆虫的持续监测以及对人类样本的基因组测序对于检测沙蒙达对人类的风险的任何变化至关重要。蒂尔斯顿-卢内尔与这项新研究无关。

paras.en: Veterinary virologist Martin Beer of the Friedrich Loeffler Institute in Germany is part of a team that has conducted several studies of the Shamonda virus, including a recent preprint on the first evidence of its presence in European sheep and goats. Beer says that the main transmission route of viruses of the Simbu serogroup are biting midges, which can rapidly spread infections, especially in the summer and autumn. “In winter the transmission cycle stops since the number of biting midges is very low and temperatures below approximately 12 degrees Celsius do not allow efficient virus replication,” he says.
paras.zh: 德国弗里德里希·洛夫勒研究所的兽医病毒学家马丁·比尔 (Martin Beer) 所在的团队对沙蒙达病毒进行了多项研究，其中包括最近发表的关于该病毒在欧洲绵羊和山羊中存在的第一个证据的预印本。比尔说，辛布血清群病毒的主要传播途径是叮咬蠓，这种蠓可以迅速传播感染，尤其是在夏季和秋季。 “在冬季，传播周期会停止，因为叮咬蠓的数量非常少，而且温度低于约 12 摄氏度，病毒无法有效复制，”他说。

paras.en: A spokesperson for the ECDC told Scientific American that the agency needs clarity regarding the transmission of the virus and the role of vectors in infecting people. Destras suggests that retrospective analyses of stored samples from immunocompromised people could identify asymptomatic infections and the true scale of Shamonda in France.
paras.zh: ECDC 的一位发言人告诉《科学美国人》，该机构需要澄清病毒的传播以及媒介在感染人类中的作用。德斯特拉斯建议，对免疫功能低下者储存的样本进行回顾性分析可以识别无症状感染者以及法国沙蒙达的真实规模。

paras.en: Beer points out that novel cases of unexplained encephalitis have occurred in immunocompromised people who were infected with other orthobunyaviruses, such as the Jamestown Canyon virus or the Cache Valley virus. More studies to analyze antibody prevalence against Shamonda in people could give a clearer picture of whether this particular virus made the leap to humans before and we just didn’t realize because no one died.
paras.zh: 比尔指出，不明原因脑炎的新病例发生在感染其他正布尼亚病毒（例如詹姆斯敦峡谷病毒或卡什谷病毒）的免疫功能低下人群中。更多的研究来分析人类中针对沙蒙达的​​抗体流行情况，可以更清楚地了解这种特定病毒是否曾在之前传播给人类，但我们只是没有意识到，因为没有人死亡。

articles.title: Sci-fi horror collides with small-town politics in John Scalzi’s Monsters of Ohio

paras.en: John Scalzi has developed a reputation in science fiction for comitting to the bit. Whether with meta-explorations of killable side characters in Redshirts or a world in which the moon literally turns into cheese in When the Moon Hits Your Eye, you can count on Scalzi seeing a concept through to its wildest implications. In his latest romp, corporate greed, lovable cows and hideous monsters converge in Richland, Ohio. It’s a small, exploited town on its last legs—but the first tentacles will be arriving shortly.
paras.zh: 约翰·斯卡尔齐因对细节的投入而在科幻小说界享有盛誉。无论是《红衫军》中对可杀死的配角的元探索，还是《当月亮击中你的眼睛时》中月亮实际上变成奶酪的世界，你都可以相信斯卡尔齐会洞察一个概念的最疯狂的含义。在他最新的嬉戏中，企业的贪婪、可爱的奶牛和可怕的怪物聚集在俄亥俄州里奇兰。这是一个被剥削的小镇，已经走到了最后的尽头，但第一批触角很快就会到来。

paras.en: Fresh off a red-eye flight after winning his fourth Hugo Award, Scalzi stopped by to chat with us about his newest novel, Monsters of Ohio.
paras.zh: 斯卡尔齐在获得第四次雨果奖后刚刚乘坐红眼航班，顺便过来和我们聊了聊他的最新小说《俄亥俄怪物》。

paras.en: [An edited transcript of the interview follows.]
paras.zh: [编辑后的采访记录如下。]

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: If you had to pitch Monsters of Ohio to someone who has never read a John Scalzi novel, what would you say?
paras.zh: 如果你必须向从未读过约翰·斯卡尔齐小说的人推销《俄亥俄怪物》，你会说什么？

paras.en: I describe it as “cozy Cronenberg.” The slightly longer version of that is “Stephen King and Nora Ephron are made to violently kiss.”
paras.zh: 我将其描述为“舒适的柯南伯格”。稍微长一点的版本是“史蒂芬·金和诺拉·艾芙隆注定要猛烈地接吻。”

paras.en: When you last sat down with us, you described your niche in contemporary science fiction as taking “a really absurd idea and then [trying] to apply real life to it.” Monsters of Ohio seems to be no exception. How did we get here?
paras.zh: 当您上次与我们坐下来时，您将自己在当代科幻小说中的定位描述为“提出一个非常荒谬的想法，然后[尝试]将其应用到现实生活中”。俄亥俄怪物似乎也不例外。我们是怎么到这里的？

paras.en: Well, thanks to Stephen King and Stranger Things and all of that sort of stuff, we have all seen the idea of monsters in a small town, right? I thought it would be fun to take a lot of the dressing of that and put a new spin on it, where the idea was not necessarily horror but to see what some of the consequences would be if, all of a sudden, there were monsters in your town and yet you were still trying to get through the rest of your day.
paras.zh: 好吧，多亏了斯蒂芬·金和《怪奇物语》以及所有类似的东西，我们都看到了小镇上的怪物的想法，对吧？我认为对它进行大量的修饰并对其进行新的旋转会很有趣，这个想法不一定是恐怖的，而是看看如果突然之间，你的城镇里出现了怪物，但你仍然在努力度过余下的一天，会产生什么后果。

paras.en: What did your research process look like? How much digging did you do for the more scientific aspects of the book?
paras.zh: 您的研究过程是怎样的？您对这本书的更科学的方面做了多少挖掘？

paras.en: A lot of my “research” is not directed research. It is literally “Oh! I remember this one thing I read one time on the internet!” And either that comes in handy while I’m writing, or it will pop up in my head and will keep going around and around and around until I write something about it. My brain is a rat’s nest of judicial decisions, fun facts about small mammals, and lots and lots of astronomy stuff.
paras.zh: 我的很多“研究”都不是定向研究。它的字面意思是“哦！我记得我在互联网上读过一件事！”要么在我写作时派上用场，要么它会突然出现在我的脑海中，并不断地转来转去，直到我写出一些关于它的东西。我的大脑是一个充满司法判决、关于小型哺乳动物的有趣事实以及许许多多天文学知识的老鼠巢。

paras.en: I think, in many ways, I was uniquely designed to be a novelist, because when people are like, “When will you ever use that information?” I’ll be like, “Well, as it turns out, I will use it while I’m writing up a book called Monsters of Ohio.” So there you have it.
paras.zh: 我认为，在很多方面，我都是独一无二的小说家，因为当人们问，“你什么时候会使用这些信息？”我会说，“好吧，事实证明，我会在写一本名为《俄亥俄怪物》的书时使用它。”这样你就得到了。

paras.en: How important is scientific plausibility to you when writing science fiction?
paras.zh: 当你写科幻小说时，科学合理性对你来说有多重要？

paras.en: It’s very important to me that people remember that science fiction has two parts to the phrase. There is the science, but there is also the fiction. I want to get the science at least broadly correct and reasonable so that, when I step into the fiction part, you can see it as a natural extension. Now you may or may not always agree with how I’ve decided to step off into the fiction part, but you can see, at least, [how] I got there.
paras.zh: 对我来说非常重要的是，让人们记住科幻小说这个词有两个部分。有科学，但也有虚构。我想让科学至少在很大程度上是正确和合理的，这样，当我进入虚构部分时，你可以将其视为自然的延伸。现在你可能同意也可能不同意我决定进入小说部分，但至少你可以看到我[如何]到达那里。

paras.en: I am always very hesitant to call myself a hard science-fiction writer because so much of that basically requires an advanced degree—and I have a B. A. in philosophy, so all I know is how to find things. That said, I’ve always also had a real interest in science and a real interest in talking about how science interacts with our lives. And so, when you are writing a story where, you know, [highly unlikely monster shenanigans redacted by editor], you want to be able to do it in a way that is, at least, scientifically plausible. I mean, [a written event] always happens because plot, but mine is rooted in specific things that happened in the natural world, as opposed to “and then magic” or “and then gods and demons.” There’s nothing wrong with gods and demons, but, in my case, I’m a science-fiction writer, so that’s where my brain goes first.
paras.zh: 我总是很犹豫是否称自己为硬科幻小说作家，因为其中很多内容基本上都需要高级学位——而且我拥有哲学学士学位，所以我所知道的就是如何发现事物。也就是说，我一直对科学抱有真正的兴趣，并且真正有兴趣谈论科学如何与我们的生活相互作用。因此，当你在写一个故事时，你知道，[极不可能由编辑编辑的怪物恶作剧]，你希望能够以一种至少在科学上合理的方式来做到这一点。我的意思是，[书面事件]总是因为情节而发生，但我的故事植根于自然世界中发生的特定事物，而不是“然后是魔法”或“然后是神和恶魔”。神魔并没有什么问题，但就我而言，我是一个科幻小说作家，所以我的大脑首先想到的就是这个。

paras.en: Monsters of Ohio is your 20th novel, and it feels paradoxically cynical and hopeful at the same time.
paras.zh: 《俄亥俄怪物》是你的第 20 部小说，它给人一种矛盾的愤世嫉俗的感觉，同时又充满希望。

paras.en: A lot of that cynicism plus hopefulness comes out of the experience of modern life and day-to-day life.
paras.zh: 很多愤世嫉俗和希望都来自现代​​生活和日常生活的经历。

paras.en: We live in a world where there is private equity strip-mining small towns. We live in a world where the interests of the moneyed class really are at odds with the interests of the people going day-to-day. [Take] where I live right now. In this moment, we are having a huge discussion about [how] they’re going to put power lines somewhere through Darke County, [Ohio], which is also the county that’s in the book. They swear to us that [the lines] are not to power the huge data centers that are being put up in our state right now, but come on. And part of the problem is that one of the routes is literally my street.
paras.zh: 我们生活在一个充满私募股权露天采矿小镇的世界。我们生活在一个有钱阶层的利益与人们日常利益确实不一致的世界。 [拿]我现在住的地方。此时此刻，我们正在热烈讨论如何在[俄亥俄州]达克县的某个地方铺设电线，这也是书中提到的县。他们向我们发誓，[这些线路]不会为我们州目前正在建设的大型数据中心供电，但是加油。部分问题在于，其中一条路线实际上就是我的街道。

paras.en: The hopeful part is the part where the people who are dealing with the consequences of that look toward their community, look toward their friends, look toward the people around them for support, for help, for unity—all of those sorts of things. The way that I think the little guy is going to get through this is to look at his neighbors and realize that all the messaging and disinformation that is designed to keep us angry and suspicious at our neighbors is, in fact, designed to keep us angry and suspicious of our neighbors and, in fact, [that] we need our neighbors’ help and that we need to help our neighbors and support them as much as we can during this time.
paras.zh: 充满希望的部分是，那些正在应对这一后果的人们向他们的社区、向他们的朋友、向周围的人寻求支持、帮助、团结——所有这些事情。我认为这个小家伙解决这个问题的方法就是看看他的邻居，并意识到所有旨在让我们对邻居生气和怀疑的信息和虚假信息实际上都是为了让我们对邻居生气和怀疑，事实上，我们需要邻居的帮助，我们需要在这段时间帮助我们的邻居并尽可能地支持他们。

paras.en: This is already helping, because I thought the takeaway of the book was that the proverbial little people were going to get through this by exploding.
paras.zh: 这已经很有帮助了，因为我认为这本书的要点是众所周知的小人物将通过爆炸来度过难关。

paras.en: Getting to the really important questions now: You have often asked musicians to write theme songs for your books. Have you done that here?
paras.zh: 现在进入真正重要的问题：您经常要求音乐家为您的书创作主题曲。你在这里做过吗？

paras.en: I have inquiries out, which is, I think, the only thing that I can say at this time. But it would make sense to do it because the protagonist was very briefly in a very briefly famous emo band. So I would like to have that set up. Unfortunately I may have missed the window for the hardcover release, but there’s always the trade paperback release in about a year.
paras.zh: 我有一些询问，我想这是我目前唯一能说的。但这样做是有意义的，因为主角在一个非常短暂的著名情绪乐队中呆过很短的时间。所以我想进行这样的设置。不幸的是，我可能错过了精装本的发行窗口，但大约一年后总会有平装本发行。

paras.en: Chappell Roan would do a great rendition of the protagonist’s signature song, “Red Wine Massacre,” in case you’re taking suggestions.
paras.zh: 如果你接受建议的话，查普尔·罗恩（Chappell Roan）会精彩地演绎主角的招牌歌曲“红酒大屠杀”。

paras.en: I think she might be a little bit out of my price range. When you commission something like that, you do have to pay your artists, and I think Chappell Roan might be just a little pricey for a humble science-fiction author.
paras.zh: 我想她的价格可能有点超出我的承受范围。当你委托做这样的事情时，你确实必须付钱给你的艺术家，我认为查普尔·罗恩对于一个谦虚的科幻小说作家来说可能有点贵。

paras.en: What would it take to get you to write a book about someone from Michigan?
paras.zh: 怎样才能让你写一本关于密歇根州人的书？

paras.en: I would be happy to have a character from Michigan. Will my neighbors burn my house down if I do it? Possibly. But that is the risk one takes for true literature.
paras.zh: 我很高兴能有一个来自密歇根的角色。如果我这样做，邻居会烧毁我的房子吗？可能吧。但这就是真正的文学所冒的风险。

articles.title: Landmark study finds three in four NFL players die with CTE

paras.en: American football can be brutal. Scientists have long known that the hits, tackles and other collisions that are central to the sport come with health risks, but what these impacts do to the brain has been less clear. What we do know is that many footballers have died with brains that have shown evidence of chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), a disease associated with symptoms such as mood swings and dementia. But because a diagnosis requires that investigators look for damage in a person’s brain after they die, it’s unclear just how common CTE is among current or former athletes.
paras.zh: 美式足球可能很残酷。科学家们早就知道，这项运动的核心内容是击球、铲球和其他碰撞会带来健康风险，但这些影响对大脑的影响尚不清楚。我们所知道的是，许多足球运动员去世时大脑中都存在慢性创伤性脑病（CTE）的证据，这是一种与情绪波动和痴呆等症状相关的疾病。但由于诊断需要研究人员在人死后寻找大脑损伤情况，因此目前尚不清楚 CTE 在现任或前任运动员中有多常见。

paras.en: But now, in a study published in JAMA Network Open, an analysis of medical records from thousands of deceased former NFL players—including hundreds who donated their brains to science—estimates that about 75 percent of these players likely died with CTE.
paras.zh: 但现在，在《JAMA Network Open》上发表的一项研究中，对数千名已故前 NFL 球员（其中包括数百名将大脑捐献给科学的人）的医疗记录进行了分析，估计这些球员中约 75% 可能死于 CTE。

paras.en: “No other environmental or occupational exposure ever studied is known to have increased dementia risk at death by that amount,” says Yorghos Tripodis, senior author of the paper and a professor of biostatistics at Boston University.
paras.zh: 该论文的资深作者、波士顿大学生物统计学教授约尔戈斯·特里波迪斯 (Yorghos Tripodis) 表示：“据了解，迄今为止没有研究过任何其他环境或职业暴露会导致死亡时患痴呆症的风险增加如此之多。”

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The study is based on records of 2,362 former NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 and played in the league for an average of five years. Among those who donated their brains—almost 400 players—a stunning 93.5 percent had CTE. Signs of CTE in the brain can include atrophy, or tissue wasting, as well as clusters of tau protein—a symptom that is also linked to Alzheimer’s disease.
paras.zh: 该研究基于 2,362 名前 NFL 球员的记录，他们在 2008 年至 2023 年间去世，平均在联盟效力五年。在捐献大脑的近 400 名玩家中，令人震惊的是，93.5% 的人患有 CTE。大脑中 CTE 的症状包括萎缩或组织浪费，以及 tau 蛋白簇——这种症状也与阿尔茨海默病有关。

paras.en: The high incidence of CTE in those donors may reflect the sample itself: people who donate their brains to science tend to have more severe behavioral symptoms, Tripodis says. That could skew the dataset, potentially making CTE rates appear artificially high.
paras.zh: Tripodis 说，这些捐献者 CTE 的高发病率可能反映了样本本身：将大脑捐献给科学的人往往有更严重的行为症状。这可能会扭曲数据集，从而可能导致 CTE 率显得人为地偏高。

paras.en: To better estimate how common CTE might have been across all 2,362 former players in the study, Tripodis and his colleagues analyzed the medical records of donors and nondonors. The team found that people with cognitive symptoms were about five times more likely to donate their brain. Given that, the researchers recalculated their incidence estimate to find that some three in four football players in the study likely had CTE.
paras.zh: 为了更好地估计研究中所有 2,362 名前球员中 CTE 的常见程度，Tripodis 和他的同事分析了捐赠者和非捐赠者的医疗记录。研究小组发现，有认知症状的人捐献大脑的可能性大约是其他人的五倍。鉴于此，研究人员重新计算了他们的发病率估计，发现研究中大约四分之三的足球运动员可能患有 CTE。

paras.en: For comparison, among the general population, fewer than 1 percent of brains in community-based brain banks show signs of CTE, Tripodis says.
paras.zh: Tripodis 表示，相比之下，在普通人群中，社区脑库中只有不到 1% 的大脑表现出 CTE 迹象。

paras.en: The study only includes NFL players who had died, and it remains difficult, if not impossible, to diagnose CTE in living players. It is hard to say what the risk to NFL players today is, Tripodis says. The NFL has also taken steps to mitigate the risk of head injuries.
paras.zh: 该研究仅包括已去世的 NFL 球员，并且诊断活着的球员的 CTE 仍然很困难（如果不是不可能的话）。特里波迪斯说，很难说当今 NFL 球员面临的风险有多大。 NFL 还采取措施降低头部受伤的风险。

paras.en: The records may also be incomplete or imprecise. For instance, symptoms of CTE such as dementia may not be listed on death records, Tripodis says. And even if dementia is listed, it can have other—even multiple—causes.
paras.zh: 记录也可能不完整或不准确。例如，特里波迪斯说，死亡记录中可能不会列出痴呆等 CTE 症状。即使痴呆症被列出，它也可能有其他原因，甚至是多种原因。

paras.en: This study is “the best attempt so far to correct for selection bias in CTE brain bank data,” says Russell Lonser, a professor in neurological surgery at the Ohio State University, who was not involved in the study. But “it is an estimate from a model and should be read that way.”
paras.zh: 俄亥俄州立大学神经外科教授 Russell Lonser（未参与这项研究）表示，这项研究是“迄今为止纠正 CTE 脑库数据选择偏差的最佳尝试”。但“这是模型的估计，应该这样解读。”

paras.en: "Without similar men who never played contact sports, we can’t tell how much of the pathology or dementia comes from football,” Lonser says. “The 75 percent includes any CTE pathology, even early changes that may never have caused symptoms.”
paras.zh: 朗瑟说：“如果没有类似的从未参加过接触性运动的人，我们就无法判断有多少病态或痴呆症来自足球。” “75% 包括任何 CTE 病理，甚至可能从未引起症状的早期变化。”

paras.en: To better understand how football increases the risks of CTE, Lonser says, you’d need to study players, with and without symptoms, over time, along with conducting brain analyses and including a comparison group of people who had no exposure to head impacts. “Until that work is done, we won’t know how common CTE really is or what, specifically, it means for players.”
paras.zh: 朗瑟说，为了更好地了解足球如何增加 CTE 的风险，你需要随着时间的推移研究有或没有症状的球员，同时进行大脑分析，并包括一组没有受到头部撞击的人。 “在这项工作完成之前，我们不会知道 CTE 到底有多常见，也不知道它对玩家意味着什么。”

paras.en: Still, Tripodis hopes the findings will prove useful for families who have been affected by CTE and will inform current and future players of the risks involved in the sport.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，Tripodis 希望这些发现能够对受 CTE 影响的家庭有用，并让当前和未来的运动员了解这项运动所涉及的风险。

paras.en: “CTE is a preventable disease. We find, in study after study, that the more blows to the head over your lifetime, the higher the risk of CTE,” Tripodis says. “If you reduce exposure to repetitive head impacts, then you reduce the risk of CTE.”
paras.zh: “CTE 是一种可预防的疾病。我们在一项又一项的研究中发现，一生中头部受到的打击越多，患 CTE 的风险就越高，”Tripodis 说。 “如果你减少头部重复受到撞击的机会，那么你就可以降低 CTE 的风险。”

articles.title: Comets probably didn’t deliver life’s building blocks to Earth
articles.author: Skyler Ware

paras.en: The chemical building blocks that gave rise to life on Earth probably didn’t come from comets.
paras.zh: 地球上孕育生命的化学成分可能并非来自彗星。

paras.en: Most comets would have been traveling too fast and at too steep an angle to Earth for prebiotic compounds to survive impact with the planet, researchers contend October 28 in Scientific Reports. While the study doesn’t completely rule out the possibility that comets brought these molecules to Earth, it contradicts the long-standing idea that comets seeded Earth with the chemicals necessary for life to arise.
paras.zh: 研究人员在 10 月 28 日的《科学报告》中指出，大多数彗星运行速度太快，与地球的角度太陡，以至于生命起源前的化合物无法在撞击地球时幸存下来。虽然这项研究并没有完全排除彗星将这些分子带到地球的可能性，但它与长期以来的观点相矛盾，即彗星在地球上播下了生命产生所需的化学物质。

paras.en: “Even though we see that comets contain all of these molecules in really high concentrations, it’s not straightforward to go from there to saying we’re going to have all of these available for prebiotic chemistry on the surface of the Earth,” says Richard Anslow, a planetary scientist at the Met Office, the national meteorological service for the United Kingdom in Exeter.
paras.zh: 英国气象局行星科学家理查德·安斯洛（Richard Anslow）表示：“尽管我们发现彗星中含有非常高浓度的所有这些分子，但从那里到我们将在地球表面拥有可用于生命起源前化学的所有这些分子并不简单。”

paras.en: Comets carry carbon- and nitrogen-containing molecules left over from early in the solar system’s formation. These molecules can react to form biologically important compounds like sugars and DNA. Scientists have long thought that comets could have delivered these building blocks to Earth when they collided with the planet during its first billion years.
paras.zh: 彗星携带着太阳系形成早期遗留下来的含碳和氮分子。这些分子可以发生反应，形成具有重要生物学意义的化合物，如糖和 DNA。长期以来，科学家们一直认为，彗星在地球诞生的第一个十亿年期间与地球相撞时，可能将这些构件带到了地球上。

paras.en: But it’s important to revisit these ideas as our understanding of both comets and the early solar system improves, says Nicolle Zellner, a physicist at Albion College in Michigan who was not involved in the study.
paras.zh: 但随着我们对彗星和早期太阳系的了解不断加深，重新审视这些想法很重要，密歇根州阿尔比恩学院的物理学家尼科尔·泽尔纳（Nicolle Zellner）没有参与这项研究，他说。

paras.en: In the new work, Anslow and colleagues used computer simulations to predict the likelihood that a chemical called hydrogen cyanide would survive a comet’s journey through Earth’s present atmosphere and its impact with the planet’s surface. The early Earth’s atmosphere was probably much denser, so would have been even more destructive.
paras.zh: 在这项新工作中，安斯洛和同事使用计算机模拟来预测一种名为氰化氢的化学物质在彗星穿越地球现有大气层的旅程及其对地球表面的影响中幸存下来的可能性。早期地球的大气层可能密度更大，因此更具破坏性。

paras.en: The strong chemical bond between the carbon and nitrogen atoms in hydrogen cyanide can release energy that drives later chemical reactions necessary for life. It also makes the molecule particularly stable compared to other carbon-based chemicals.
paras.zh: 氰化氢中碳原子和氮原子之间的牢固化学键可以释放能量，驱动随后生命所需的化学反应。与其他碳基化学品相比，它还使该分子特别稳定。

paras.en: “It’s probably one of the more robust molecules to surviving impacts,” Anslow says. “So if things look bad for hydrogen cyanide, then we think it’s going to be much harder for other, more complicated molecules that are more likely to be broken down during these impacts.”
paras.zh: “它可能是在撞击中幸存下来的更强大的分子之一，”安斯洛说。 “因此，如果氰化氢的情况看起来很糟糕，那么我们认为对于其他更复杂的分子来说，情况会变得更加困难，因为这些分子在这些影响期间更有可能被分解。”

paras.en: Based on the simulations, a comet impact that kept hydrogen cyanide intact would be extremely unlikely, the team found. On average, the simulations suggest that only one impact would have been able to deliver a meaningful amount of hydrogen cyanide to the planet’s surface over more than a billion years. For hydrogen cyanide to survive the crash, the comet would have to be larger than 100 meters across, slow moving and traveling at an oblique angle to Earth.
paras.zh: 研究小组发现，根据模拟，彗星撞击使氰化氢保持完整的可能性极小。平均而言，模拟表明，在十亿多年的时间里，只有一次撞击就能向地球表面释放大量氰化氢。为了让氰化氢在撞击中幸存下来，彗星的直径必须大于 100 米，缓慢移动，并以与地球倾斜的角度行进。

paras.en: A comet that met those narrow criteria would also have had to crash into land, rather than an ocean, to kick off any biologically useful chemistry. If the comet landed in the ocean, any hydrogen cyanide that survived would be diluted too quickly to trigger those reactions.
paras.zh: 满足这些狭窄标准的彗星也必须撞击陆地，而不是海洋，才能引发任何对生物有用的化学反应。如果彗星降落在海洋中，任何幸存的氰化氢都会被稀释得太快而无法引发这些反应。

paras.en: While still improbable, comets may have been more likely to deliver carbon-based molecules to Mars than to Earth, the simulations showed. Mars’ thinner atmosphere and smaller size meant that comets would impact at lower speeds. That could mean that more compounds could survive the collision.
paras.zh: 模拟显示，尽管可能性仍然不大，但彗星可能更有可能将碳基分子运送到火星而不是地球。火星的大气层较稀薄，尺寸较小，这意味着彗星将以较低的速度撞击。这可能意味着更多的化合物可以在碰撞中幸存下来。

paras.en: If Earth’s carbon-based chemicals didn’t come from comets, they may have come from carbon-rich asteroids called carbonaceous chondrites, says Gordon Osinski, a planetary geologist at Western University in London, Canada, who was not involved in the study. Other sources might have included volcanoes and hydrothermal vents.
paras.zh: 加拿大伦敦西部大学的行星地质学家戈登·奥辛斯基（未参与这项研究）表示，如果地球上的碳基化学物质不是来自彗星，它们可能来自富含碳的小行星，即碳质球粒陨石。其他来源可能包括火山和热液喷口。

paras.en: The study “definitely will make people think twice about comets being the originator for the delivery of organics,” Osinski says. “I hope other people will try to reproduce these results [and] then potentially try something similar with carbonaceous chondrites as well.”
paras.zh: 奥辛斯基说，这项研究“肯定会让人们重新思考彗星是有机物输送的起源”。 “我希望其他人能够尝试重现这些结果，然后也可能尝试用碳质球粒陨石进行类似的尝试。”

articles.title: Why do flamingos dance while they eat? This scientist found out
articles.author: Anna Mattson

paras.en: On a family trip to Atlanta, Víctor Ortega Jiménez spent time taking pictures and videos of flamingos as they fed in their pond. It wasn’t to admire their long legs or flamboyant pink color. Instead, he noticed the “beautiful” ripples spreading across the water as the birds ate under the surface. But he didn’t know why the waves were happening.
paras.zh: 在一次前往亚特兰大的家庭旅行中，维克多·奥尔特加·希门尼斯 (Víctor Ortega Jiménez) 花时间拍摄了火烈鸟在池塘里进食的照片和视频。这并不是为了欣赏他们的长腿或艳丽的粉色。相反，他注意到当鸟类在水面下进食时，“美丽”的涟漪在水面上蔓延。但他不知道为什么会出现波浪。

paras.en: It took “more than four years to answer that question,” says Ortega Jiménez, of the University of California, Berkeley. “But I think the answer was fascinating.”
paras.zh: 加州大学伯克利分校的奥尔特加·希门尼斯说，“花了四年多的时间才回答这个问题”。 “但我认为答案很有趣。”

paras.en: Ortega Jiménez’s focus is biomechanics, or the study of how mechanics applies to animal movement and structure. His goal is to understand how animal behaviors might lead to human-made engineering feats.
paras.zh: 奥尔特加·希门尼斯的研究重点是生物力学，即研究力学如何应用于动物运动和结构。他的目标是了解动物行为如何导致人造工程壮举。

paras.en: He discovered that, by retracting their heads, flamingos produce vortexlike traps with water to scoop up algae. They stomp around — or dance, if you will — amplifying the vortex. The series of motions brings the food to their crooked beaks. The beaks then filter in food, releasing silt and mud.
paras.zh: 他发现，通过缩回头部，火烈鸟会用水产生漩涡状的陷阱来舀起藻类。他们跺脚——或者跳舞，如果你愿意的话——放大了漩涡。这一系列动作将食物送到它们弯曲的嘴里。然后喙过滤食物，释放淤泥和泥土。

paras.en: The impressive process can weed out particles the size of a single cell. This kind of self-cleaning filter for extremely small particles can be applied to remove microplastics and so-called forever chemicals called PFAS from water, Ortega Jiménez says.
paras.zh: 这个令人印象深刻的过程可以清除单个细胞大小的颗粒。 Ortega Jiménez 表示，这种针对极小颗粒的自清洁过滤器可用于去除水中的微塑料和所谓的永久化学物质 PFAS。

paras.en: “Nature is always full of secrets,” he says. “And I think that’s the riddle that keeps me going, trying to understand nature. That’s my way to see science: by observation and trying to be inspired and trying to solve a problem.”
paras.zh: “大自然总是充满秘密，”他说。 “我认为这就是让我继续前进、努力理解自然的谜团。这就是我看待科学的方式：通过观察、试图受到启发并试图解决问题。”

articles.title: Three-quarters of NFL football players may end up with CTE
articles.author: Aimee Cunningham

paras.en: An estimated three-quarters of NFL players who died in a 16-year period had the devastating neurogenerative disease called CTE.
paras.zh: 据估计，在 16 年内死亡的 NFL 球员中有四分之三患有名为 CTE 的破坏性神经再生疾病。

paras.en: Back in 2017, researchers reported that an estimated 99 percent of former NFL players developed CTE, or chronic traumatic encephalopathy, from an analysis of donated brains. But the families who provided the donations may have done so because their football-playing relatives had symptoms related to CTE, which could skew the results. A new study, which accounts for this potential bias, estimates that nearly 75 percent of former NFL players have CTE at death. It’s the first population-level estimate for NFL players, researchers report October 28 in JAMA Network Open.
paras.zh: 早在 2017 年，研究人员就报告称，根据对捐赠大脑的分析，估计 99% 的前 NFL 球员患有 CTE（慢性创伤性脑病）。但提供捐款的家庭可能这样做是因为他们踢足球的亲戚有与 CTE 相关的症状，这可能会扭曲结果。一项新的研究解释了这种潜在的偏差，估计近 75% 的前 NFL 球员在死亡时患有 CTE。研究人员于 10 月 28 日在 JAMA Network Open 上报告称，这是对 NFL 球员的首次人口水平估计。

paras.en: The development of CTE is linked to repeated blows to the head over time. The disease can occur in people who play contact sports, experience intimate partner violence or engage in military combat. A study of American football players suggests that the longer the duration of repeated head trauma, the higher the risk of CTE and the more severe the condition. During life, people who are later diagnosed with CTE can experience symptoms including memory issues, difficulty concentrating, depression and poor impulse control.
paras.zh: CTE 的发生与头部反复受到打击有关。这种疾病可能发生在从事接触性运动、遭受亲密伴侣暴力或参加军事战斗的人身上。一项针对美国橄榄球运动员的研究表明，反复头部外伤的持续时间越长，发生 CTE 的风险就越高，病情也越严重。在生活中，后来被诊断出患有 CTE 的人可能会出现记忆问题、注意力难以集中、抑郁和冲动控制能力差等症状。

paras.en: A brain protein called tau, which usually helps nerve cells communicate and performs other jobs, goes awry in CTE. Brains with the disease are snarled with irregular, damaging clumps of the protein. The condition is diagnosed after death, during an autopsy, and has been identified most frequently among American football players.
paras.zh: 一种名为 tau 的大脑蛋白通常帮助神经细胞沟通并执行其他工作，但在 CTE 中却出现了问题。患有这种疾病的大脑中充满了不规则的、具有破坏性的蛋白质团块。这种情况是在死后尸检过程中被诊断出来的，并且在美国橄榄球运动员中最常见。

paras.en: The new study, by a Boston University research team, included all previous NFL players who passed away from January 2008 through December 2023. The more than 2,300 players included almost 400 with samples in the university’s UNITE Brain Bank, with the remainder identified from records in the U.S. National Death Index. The research team determined that families of NFL players who had CTE-related symptoms in life were five times more likely to donate their relative’s brain than families whose relative did not experience symptoms. Taking that into consideration, the team landed on a population-level CTE estimate for NFL players of 74.5 percent.
paras.zh: 波士顿大学研究小组进行的这项新研究涵盖了 2008 年 1 月至 2023 年 12 月期间去世的所有 NFL 球员。这 2,300 多名球员中包括近 400 名球员，样本保存在该大学的 UNITE 脑库中，其余的则从美国国家死亡指数的记录中确定。研究小组确定，在生活中出现 CTE 相关症状的 NFL 球员的家庭捐献其亲属大脑的可能性是其亲属没有出现症状的家庭的五倍。考虑到这一点，该团队对 NFL 球员的人口水平 CTE 估计为 74.5%。

paras.en: The research team notes that determining the true prevalence of CTE is important to understanding the public health impact of the disease.
paras.zh: 研究小组指出，确定 CTE 的真实患病率对于了解该疾病对公共健康的影响非常重要。

articles.title: Scientists Found a Blood Signature Linked to 23% Lower Risk of Death
articles.author: Esra Öz

paras.en: Remembering everything you ate last week can be difficult, but your blood may keep its own record: traces of how your body processed those meals.
paras.zh: 记住你上周吃的所有东西可能很困难，但你的血液可能会保留自己的记录：你的身体如何处理这些食物的痕迹。

paras.en: Scientists have found that a blood signature tied to Mediterranean-style eating is linked to risk of dying years later. In a study involving 14,584 people in Spain and the United States, groups with higher signature scores had a lower risk of death during follow-up.
paras.zh: 科学家发现，与地中海式饮食相关的血液特征与数年后死亡的风险有关。在一项涉及西班牙和美国 14,584 人的研究中，签名得分较高的群体在随访期间死亡风险较低。

paras.en: The research, involving scientists from the University of Navarra, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, and other institutions, offers a way to study diet without relying only on what people remember eating.
paras.zh: 这项研究涉及来自纳瓦拉大学、哈佛大学 T.H.陈公共卫生学院和其他机构提供了一种研究饮食的方法，而不仅仅是依赖人们记忆中的饮食。

paras.en: Mediterranean-style eating emphasizes vegetables, fruit, legumes, nuts, fish, and olive oil, while limiting red and processed meat. This pattern has been linked to various health benefits, but measuring how closely someone follows it usually involves dietary questionnaires.
paras.zh: 地中海式饮食强调蔬菜、水果、豆类、坚果、鱼和橄榄油，同时限制红肉和加工肉类。这种模式与各种健康益处有关，但衡量人们遵循这种模式的程度通常涉及饮食调查问卷。

paras.en: "Questionnaires depend on what people remember and report, so they are prone to misclassification," University of Navarra epidemiologist Estefanía Toledo told ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: 纳瓦拉大学流行病学家埃斯特凡尼亚·托莱多 (Estefanía Toledo) 告诉 ScienceAlert，“调查问卷取决于人们记忆和报告的内容，因此很容易出现错误分类。”

paras.en: As the body processes food, it produces or transforms small molecules called metabolites. These can carry information about both what we eat and how our bodies respond to it.
paras.zh: 当身体处理食物时，它会产生或转化称为代谢物的小分子。它们可以携带有关我们吃什么以及我们的身体如何反应的信息。

paras.en: The researchers examined a pattern of 67 metabolites, mostly lipids (fat-related molecules). Developed in 2020, the signature had previously been associated with Mediterranean diet adherence and cardiovascular disease risk. The new study investigated its relationship with long-term mortality.
paras.zh: 研究人员检查了 67 种代谢物的模式，其中大部分是脂质（与脂肪相关的分子）。该签名于 2020 年开发，此前曾与地中海饮食依从性和心血管疾病风险相关。这项新研究调查了其与长期死亡率的关系。

paras.en: Many of those fats echo the diet's staples. In earlier work, some tracked closely with olive oil intake, while others are long-chain fatty acids found in nuts and fish.
paras.zh: 其中许多脂肪与饮食中的主食相呼应。在早期的研究中，一些与橄榄油的摄入量密切相关，而另一些则是坚果和鱼类中发现的长链脂肪酸。

paras.en: The team started with blood samples collected from 1,880 participants upon joining a Spanish dietary trial called PREDIMED. These were older adults who had no cardiovascular disease when they enrolled but were at high risk of developing it.
paras.zh: 该团队首先从 1,880 名参加名为 PREDIMED 的西班牙饮食试验的参与者身上收集了血液样本。这些老年人在入组时并未患有心血管疾病，但患心血管疾病的风险很高。

paras.en: Over roughly 13 years of follow-up, people in the highest third of signature scores had a 23 percent lower risk of death than those in the lowest third, after accounting for factors including age, smoking, body mass index, and existing health conditions.
paras.zh: 经过大约 13 年的跟踪调查，在考虑了年龄、吸烟、体重指数和现有健康状况等因素后，签名得分最高三分之一的人的死亡风险比最低三分之一的人低 23%。

paras.en: The researchers then examined data from 12,704 participants in three long-running US studies, followed for an average of 25 years.
paras.zh: 随后，研究人员检查了美国三项长期研究中 12,704 名参与者的数据，平均跟踪时间为 25 年。

paras.en: The association appeared again: Participants in the highest fifth of signature scores had a 23 percent lower risk of death than those in the lowest fifth.
paras.zh: 这种关联再次出现：签名得分最高五分之一的参与者的死亡风险比最低五分之一的参与者低 23%。

paras.en: In the Spanish group, the association remained largely intact after accounting for self-reported adherence to the Mediterranean diet. Toledo explained that the signature may also capture how each person's body absorbs and handles food.
paras.zh: 在西班牙群体中，在考虑了自我报告的地中海饮食坚持情况后，这种关联基本上保持不变。托莱多解释说，该签名还可以捕捉每个人的身体如何吸收和处理食物。

paras.en: The authors suggest a blood test like this might eventually help doctors spot the people who stand to gain most from changing how they eat.
paras.zh: 作者认为，这样的血液测试最终可能会帮助医生发现那些从改变饮食方式中获益最多的人。

paras.en: The results can't, however, tell someone how many years they have left.
paras.zh: 然而，结果并不能告诉某人他们还剩多少年。

paras.en: "It indicates differences in risk between groups, not an individual's lifespan," Toledo said.
paras.zh: 托莱多说：“它表明了群体之间风险的差异，而不是个人的寿命。”

paras.en: Although PREDIMED was a randomized dietary trial, this analysis of the blood signature and mortality was observational, comparing people's existing scores with what happened to them later. It cannot establish that raising someone's signature score would extend their life.
paras.zh: 尽管 PREDIMED 是一项随机饮食试验，但对血液特征和死亡率的分析是观察性的，将人们现有的分数与后来发生的情况进行比较。它不能确定提高某人的签名分数会延长他们的寿命。

paras.en: Scores measured at the start of the trial and after one year, along with their average, were associated with mortality, while changes in the signature over that first year of intervention were not.
paras.zh: 试验开始时和一年后测量的分数及其平均值与死亡率相关，而干预第一年的特征变化则不然。

paras.en: The findings suggest the signature may reflect longer-term eating habits and metabolic health, although it's uncertain whether one year is too short to capture the effects of dietary changes.
paras.zh: 研究结果表明，这一特征可能反映了长期的饮食习惯和代谢健康，尽管不确定一年是否太短而无法捕捉饮食变化的影响。

paras.en: Before the approach could become a routine blood test, it would need to be tested in more diverse populations, including people of different ages and health backgrounds.
paras.zh: 在该方法成为常规血液检测之前，需要在更多样化的人群中进行测试，包括不同年龄和健康背景的人。

paras.en: The US participants were health professionals "who are mostly white and relatively healthy," Toledo told ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: 托莱多告诉 ScienceAlert，美国参与者是健康专业人士，“他们大多是白人，相对健康”。

paras.en: Researchers would also need to show that the signature improves risk prediction beyond established risk factors.
paras.zh: 研究人员还需要证明该签名可以改善风险预测，超越既定的风险因素。

paras.en: The research has been published in The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition.
paras.zh: 该研究发表在《美国临床营养学杂志》上。

articles.title: Your Brain Seems to Stretch Time While You're Learning a New Movement
articles.author: Esra Öz

paras.en: A tennis player might describe the ball seeming to slow down just before a shot. A musician might feel time passing differently when absorbed in a performance. Researchers are investigating whether preparing to move helps shape these changes in our experience of time.
paras.zh: 网球运动员可能会描述球在击球前似乎减慢了速度。当音乐家全神贯注于表演时，时间的流逝可能会有所不同。研究人员正在调查准备搬家是否有助于塑造我们时间体验的这些变化。

paras.en: One way to find out is to ask people how long a brief light stays on. A light can be visible for a fixed amount of time, but a person's judgment of its duration may shift, especially while they are preparing to reach toward a target.
paras.zh: 找出答案的一种方法是询问人们短暂的灯亮多久。光可以在固定的时间内可见，但人们对其持续时间的判断可能会发生变化，特别是当他们准备到达目标时。

paras.en: A study published in iScience found that this shift can develop with practice. As participants repeated a reaching task, they became quicker to begin moving. Alongside that improvement, they increasingly judged brief lights shown before the movement as lasting longer.
paras.zh: 《iScience》上发表的一项研究发现，这种转变可以通过实践来发展。当参与者重复执行一项到达任务时，他们开始移动的速度会更快。除了这一改进之外，他们越来越认为运动前显示的短暂灯光持续时间更长。

paras.en: "The effect was large: participants perceived stimuli as lasting 25% longer than a reference duration, which is a substantially sized distortion by illusory standards," cognitive neuroscientist Nicola Binetti of Italy's University of Rome Tor Vergata told ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: 意大利罗马托尔维加塔大学的认知神经科学家尼古拉·比内蒂 (Nicola Binetti) 告诉 ScienceAlert：“效果很大：参与者认为刺激的持续时间比参考持续时间长 25%，按照虚幻的标准来看，这是一个相当大的扭曲。”

paras.en: Earlier evidence connecting movement and timing gave the team reason to expect that practicing a movement would alter duration judgments. But practice didn't bring those judgments closer to the reference.
paras.zh: 早期将动作和时间联系起来的证据让团队有理由相信练习动作会改变持续时间的判断。但实践并没有使这些判断更接近参考。

paras.en: "What we did not expect was for practice to make the distortion stronger, rather than reduce it," Binetti said.
paras.zh: 比内蒂说：“我们没想到练习会加剧而不是减少失真。”

paras.en: The team recruited 40 right-handed adults to reach toward targets shown on a screen. Half reached left or right, while the other half reached toward a nearby or more distant target.
paras.zh: 该团队招募了 40 名惯用右手的成年人来触碰屏幕上显示的目标。一半向左或向右伸出，而另一半向附近或更远的目标伸出。

paras.en: Participants moved their right index finger across a surface beneath the screen, which hid their hand from view. A beep signaled when to move. After each attempt, the screen showed where their finger had landed.
paras.zh: 参与者将右手食指移过屏幕下方的表面，这样他们的手就看不见了。蜂鸣声表示何时移动。每次尝试后，屏幕都会显示他们的手指落地的位置。

paras.en: They also had a second task. Before moving, they watched a circle briefly light up. After the movement, they judged whether it remained illuminated longer or shorter than a reference duration of 0.84 seconds they had learned beforehand.
paras.zh: 他们还有第二个任务。在移动之前，他们看到一个圆圈短暂地亮起。运动结束后，他们判断其保持照明的时间是否长于或短于他们事先了解到的参考持续时间 0.84 秒。

paras.en: In some trials, the target appeared in advance, allowing participants to prepare their reach while waiting for the beep. In others, its location was revealed only when the beep sounded. A separate condition tested duration judgments without reaching.
paras.zh: 在一些试验中，目标提前出现，让参与者在等待蜂鸣声的同时做好准备。在其他情况下，只有当蜂鸣声响起时，它的位置才会被揭示。单独条件测试持续时间判断未达到。

paras.en: Knowing the target's location beforehand made the light appear to last longer, on average, than in either of the other conditions.
paras.zh: 平均而言，提前知道目标位置使得光线看起来比其他任何条件下持续时间更长。

paras.en: The more revealing relationship emerged across repeated attempts. Participants gradually began moving sooner after the beep and increasingly judged the lights as lasting longer.
paras.zh: 经过反复尝试，更具启发性的关系出现了。参与者在听到蜂鸣声后逐渐开始移动，并且越来越认为灯光持续时间更长。

paras.en: The speed-up was most pronounced when participants had to wait until the beep to discover the target's location, but the two changes tracked each other in both conditions.
paras.zh: 当参与者必须等到发出蜂鸣声才能发现目标位置时，加速最为明显，但这两种变化在两种情况下都是相互跟踪的。

paras.en: People whose movement initiation improved more also tended to show a greater increase in perceived duration. How accurately their finger landed didn't explain the overall shift.
paras.zh: 运动发起能力改善较多的人也往往表现出感知持续时间的更大增加。他们的手指落地的准确程度并不能解释整体的转变。

paras.en: "In a way, our brain uses the moment we intend to act as a reference for judging how long things around us last," Binetti explained.
paras.zh: 比内蒂解释说：“在某种程度上，我们的大脑利用我们打算行动的那一刻作为判断我们周围事物持续多久的参考。”

paras.en: The researchers also examined electrical brain activity using electrodes placed on the scalp, a technique called electroencephalography (EEG).
paras.zh: 研究人员还使用放置在头皮上的电极检查脑电活动，这种技术称为脑电图（EEG）。

paras.en: Their analysis linked the altered duration judgments to activity during two stages: while the light was visible and its duration was being processed, and after it disappeared, when that information was being used to form a judgment.
paras.zh: 他们的分析将改变的持续时间判断与两个阶段的活动联系起来：当光可见且其持续时间正在被处理时，以及在光消失后，当该信息被用来形成判断时。

paras.en: During the first stage, the relevant activity patterns were associated with planning a specific movement. Afterward, in the group that reached left or right, the patterns reflected broader involvement in preparing to move. A similar trend in the near-or-far group didn't reach statistical significance.
paras.zh: 在第一阶段，相关的活动模式与规划特定的动作相关联。随后，在向左或向右移动的小组中，这些模式反映出更广泛的参与准备移动。近组或远组的类似趋势并未达到统计显着性。

paras.en: Previous research has explored connections between movement-related brain processes and time perception. The new study adds a view of how this relationship evolves with practice.
paras.zh: 先前的研究探索了与运动相关的大脑过程和时间感知之间的联系。这项新研究增加了这种关系如何随着实践而演变的观点。

paras.en: Binetti said similar mechanisms could play a role in skilled activities such as sports and music. However, those activities were not directly tested in this study.
paras.zh: 比内蒂表示，类似的机制可以在体育和音乐等技能活动中发挥作用。然而，本研究并未直接测试这些活动。

paras.en: The study can't prove that faster preparation causes time expansion. Motivation, reward expectations, or other changes during practice could contribute to both. The EEG analysis also averaged trials, preventing the researchers from tracking how relevant brain activity changed with each repetition.
paras.zh: 该研究无法证明更快的准备会导致时间延长。动机、奖励期望或练习过程中的其他变化可能对两者都有影响。脑电图分析还对试验进行平均，从而阻止研究人员跟踪每次重复时相关的大脑活动如何变化。

paras.en: The findings nevertheless suggest that even a simple judgment of duration may be intertwined with an upcoming action. As we become more ready to move, the brief events we see beforehand may come to feel longer.
paras.zh: 然而，研究结果表明，即使是简单的持续时间判断也可能与即将采取的行动交织在一起。当我们变得更加准备好行动时，我们之前看到的短暂事件可能会变得更长。

paras.en: The research has been published in iScience.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在 iScience 上。

articles.title: LA's Eaton Fire Exposed 7 Million Residents to Lead 80 Times Above Normal Levels
articles.author: Jess Cockerill

paras.en: When the Santa Ana wind pushed flames from Eaton Canyon into Altadena on 7 January 2025, it quickly escalated into one of the most destructive fires in California's history.
paras.zh: 2025 年 1 月 7 日，圣安娜风将火焰从伊顿峡谷吹入阿尔塔迪纳，迅速升级为加州历史上最具破坏性的火灾之一。

paras.en: By January 9, plumes of smoke blanketed around 7 million Los Angeles residents in air laden with lead roughly 80 times above normal atmospheric levels for 24 hours.
paras.zh: 截至 1 月 9 日，烟雾笼罩了约 700 万洛杉矶居民，空气中的铅含量比正常大气水平高出约 80 倍，持续 24 小时。

paras.en: That's one of the major findings from a new study published in Science Advances, led by atmospheric chemists Haroula Baliaka and Nga Ng at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech).
paras.zh: 这是加州理工学院 (Caltech) 大气化学家 Haroula Baliaka 和 Nga Ng 领导的一项发表在 Science Advances 上的新研究的主要发现之一。

paras.en: Their research reveals just how laden with toxic metals those urban fire smoke plumes were. As well as lead, the smoke contained high concentrations of chlorine, bromine, zinc, copper, and arsenic.
paras.zh: 他们的研究揭示了城市火灾烟雾中含有多少有毒金属。除铅外，烟雾还含有高浓度的氯、溴、锌、铜和砷。

paras.en: The study also highlights potentially distinct health risks from fires that enter urban landscapes compared to those that burn in wildlands like forests and grasslands.
paras.zh: 该研究还强调，与森林和草原等荒地燃烧的火灾相比，进入城市景观的火灾可能带来明显的健康风险。

paras.en: "Unlike the wildfire smoke that has been the focus of decades of air quality research, this plume originated primarily from burning homes, vehicles, and infrastructure, a fundamentally different fuel with a distinct chemical signature," writes the team.
paras.zh: 研究小组写道：“与几十年来空气质量研究焦点的野火烟雾不同，这种烟羽主要源自燃烧的房屋、车辆和基础设施，这是一种完全不同的燃料，具有独特的化学特征。”

paras.en: More than 9,000 structures in the area burned, along with electronics and vehicles. Together, these fuel sources contributed airborne chemicals to the smoke plume that coated the Los Angeles basin for days.
paras.zh: 该地区 9,000 多座建筑物以及电子产品和车辆被烧毁。这些燃料源共同导致了空气中的化学物质，形成了覆盖洛杉矶盆地数天的烟雾。

paras.en: Directly south of the fire, a Caltech air composition monitoring facility in Pico Rivera detected real-time details of the air pollution as the situation unfolded.
paras.zh: 就在火灾以南，皮科里维拉的加州理工学院空气成分监测设施随着事态的发展实时检测到空气污染的细节。

paras.en: Air quality was at its worst in the first two days of the fire, with people in eastern LA and the San Gabriel Valley affected by the highest 24-hour average lead concentrations.
paras.zh: 火灾发生的前两天空气质量最差，洛杉矶东部和圣盖博谷的人们受到24小时平均铅浓度最高的影响。

paras.en: "Under typical conditions, daily lead at Pico Rivera averages just 0.6 nanograms per cubic meter. Overlaying daily lead maps with census data reveals the scale of exposure: On 9 January, approximately 7 million residents experienced concentrations exceeding 50 nanograms per cubic meter," Baliaka and team report.
paras.zh: “在典型条件下，皮科里维拉的每日铅平均含量仅为每立方米 0.6 纳克。将每日铅地图与人口普查数据叠加可以揭示暴露的规模：1 月 9 日，大约 700 万居民的铅浓度超过每立方米 50 纳克，”Baliaka 和团队报告。

paras.en: "Notably, as peak concentrations declined with the transition from structural to wildland burning, total population exposed continued to rise as the plume dispersed across the basin."
paras.zh: “值得注意的是，随着从结构性燃烧过渡到荒地燃烧，峰值浓度下降，随着羽流分散到整个盆地，暴露的总人口继续增加。”

paras.en: Similar results were recently reported by a team from the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), whose data came from monitoring stations on the UCLA campus in Westwood, and in Huntington Park.
paras.zh: 加州大学洛杉矶分校 (UCLA) 的一个团队最近报告了类似的结果，其数据来自加州大学洛杉矶分校韦斯特伍德校区和亨廷顿公园的监测站。

paras.en: The Caltech researchers also compared their results with data from a wildfire that occurred almost exclusively in vegetated wildlands in Riverside in 2024, about four months prior.
paras.zh: 加州理工学院的研究人员还将他们的结果与 2024 年（大约四个月前）几乎完全发生在河滨植被荒地的野火数据进行了比较。

paras.en: Compared to the Riverside fire, the Los Angeles Eaton plume contained 50 times the concentration of lead, along with 7 times the concentration of the halogens chlorine and bromine, 4 times the levels of zinc, and 3 times the levels of copper and arsenic.
paras.zh: 与河滨火灾相比，洛杉矶伊顿羽流中铅的浓度是其50倍，卤素氯和溴的浓度是其7倍，锌的含量是其4倍，铜和砷的含量是其3倍。

paras.en: Many of the houses in Altadena are early-to-mid 20th century builds, dating from a time when lead paints and brominated flame retardants were commonly used. That could explain why the Eaton fire plumes were so particularly toxic.
paras.zh: 阿尔塔迪纳的许多房屋都是 20 世纪早期至中期建造的，其历史可以追溯到普遍使用含铅油漆和溴化阻燃剂的时代。这可以解释为什么伊顿火羽的毒性如此之大。

paras.en: The health consequences for people who were exposed to this smoke remain unknown.
paras.zh: 接触这种烟雾的人的健康后果仍不清楚。

paras.en: The researchers are also concerned about the ongoing effects these contaminants have in the long term, after settling across playgrounds, watersheds, and farmlands.
paras.zh: 研究人员还担心这些污染物在游乐场、流域和农田中沉积后所产生的长期持续影响。

paras.en: "There is an urgent call for epidemiological studies to explore the health outcomes associated with these exposures, particularly in children and other vulnerable populations," Baliaka and team write.
paras.zh: 巴利卡和团队写道：“迫切需要进行流行病学研究，探讨与这些接触相关的健康结果，特别是儿童和其他弱势群体。”

paras.en: "While the toxicity of chronic exposure to individual elements (e.g., neurotoxicity of lead or carcinogenicity of arsenic) is well established, far less is known about
paras.zh: “虽然长期接触单个元素的毒性（例如铅的神经毒性或砷的致癌性）已得到充分证实，但人们对这种毒性知之甚少。

paras.en: the consequences of these short-duration but high-intensity exposures, as well as the cumulative effects of simultaneous exposure to complex mixtures."
paras.zh: 这些短期但高强度暴露的后果，以及同时暴露于复杂混合物的累积效应。”

paras.en: Very few studies have documented the effects of urban fires like this one, yet the evidence suggests disasters like this are only going to become more frequent and severe.
paras.zh: 很少有研究记录像这样的城市火灾的影响，但有证据表明，这样的灾难只会变得更加频繁和严重。

paras.en: "As climate change and urban expansion drive more fires into cities, the question is not whether another urban firestorm will occur," Baliaka and team warn.
paras.zh: 巴利卡和团队警告说：“随着气候变化和城市扩张导致更多火灾进入城市，问题不在于是否会发生另一场城市火灾风暴。”

paras.en: "What remains to be seen is what we will have learned from the previous ones and whether monitoring and emergency response systems can adapt fast enough to characterize these emissions and their exposure risk."
paras.zh: “还有待观察的是我们将从之前的事件中学到什么，以及监测和应急响应系统是否能够足够快地适应这些排放及其暴露风险。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Science Advances.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《科学进展》上。

articles.title: Smaller EV batteries, longer range? Scientists may have found a way

paras.en: Smaller EV batteries, longer range? Scientists may have found a way
paras.zh: 电动汽车电池更小，续航里程更长？科学家可能找到了方法

paras.en: - The Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST)
paras.zh: - 韩国科学技术院 (KAIST)

paras.en: - Scientists have developed a new technology that could make electric vehicle batteries smaller, lighter, and longer-lasting, potentially allowing cars to travel farther on a single charge. By borrowing precision manufacturing techniques from computer chip production, they found a way to prevent damaging lithium buildup that has held back next-generation batteries.
paras.zh: - 科学家们开发出了一种新技术，可以使电动汽车电池变得更小、更轻、更耐用，有可能让汽车一次充电可以行驶更远的距离。通过借鉴计算机芯片生产中的精密制造技术，他们找到了一种方法来防止锂积聚造成的损害，而锂积聚已阻碍了下一代电池的发展。

paras.en: Researchers in South Korea have developed a new technology that could lead to smaller, lighter electric vehicle (EV) batteries capable of delivering longer driving ranges on a single charge. Scientists at KAIST have found a way to address a major weakness of anode-free batteries, which eliminate conventional materials such as graphite to reduce battery size and weight. Although these batteries can store more energy in less space, their lifespan is often limited by the formation of sharp lithium structures during charging. The researchers tackled this problem by adapting precision manufacturing techniques from the semiconductor industry, allowing lithium to accumulate more evenly while encouraging the development of a durable protective layer.
paras.zh: 韩国研究人员开发了一项新技术，可以生产更小、更轻的电动汽车 (EV) 电池，一次充电即可提供更长的行驶里程。韩国科学技术院的科学家们找到了一种方法来解决无阳极电池的一个主要弱点，该电池消除了石墨等传统材料，以减小电池的尺寸和重量。尽管这些电池可以在更小的空间内存储更多的能量，但它们的寿命通常受到充电过程中尖锐锂结构形成的限制。研究人员通过采用半导体行业的精密制造技术来解决这个问题，使锂更均匀地积累，同时鼓励耐用保护层的开发。

paras.en: On September 22, KAIST (President Choongsik Bae) announced the breakthrough by a collaborative team led by Professors Jinwoo Lee and Hee-Tae Jung of its Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering. The project also involved scientists from Kyungpook National University (President Heo Young-woo) and the National NanoFab Center (President Park Heung Soo). By applying extremely precise fabrication methods traditionally used to manufacture semiconductor devices, the researchers developed an approach that extends the operating life of anode-free batteries without significantly increasing their size or weight.
